claims.text: Mechanical alloying followed by spark plasma sintering is a viable route for synthesizing bulk refractory high-entropy alloys.
AI-based process-parameter optimization can enable large-scale synthesis of RHEA–Cu composites with stable and uniform microstructures.
RHEA–Cu powder mixtures are prone to segregation because of positive mixing enthalpies between refractory elements and copper.
Data-driven selection of milling speed, milling time, and ball-to-powder ratio can produce uniform dispersion at larger scales.
Data-driven selection of SPS heating rate, maximum temperature, and hold time can control interdiffusion in RHEA–Cu composites.
A controlled mechanical-alloying environment can minimize contamination.
Machine-learning-optimized short, high-temperature SPS cycles can provide reproducible industrial scale-up.
Mechanical alloying can turn refractory-element and copper powders into a homogeneous feedstock.
A mechanically alloyed homogeneous feedstock suppresses segregation and microstructural heterogeneity during sintering.
Precisely tuned processing time and temperature reduce uncontrolled interdiffusion and phase separation.
Rapid SPS kinetics promote uniform densification and retention of a fine-grained microstructure.
The proposed process will reduce compositional segregation and produce stable RHEA–Cu microstructures suitable for nuclear-reactor environments.
The proposed process will improve the mechanical and thermal properties of RHEA–Cu composites.
Conventional melting or other high-temperature techniques often cause microstructural inhomogeneity and excessive copper segregation in refractory alloys.
The success of machine-learning parameter optimization depends on the availability of sufficiently accurate training data.
Process success may vary across refractory–Cu compositions and at extreme industrial scales.
Exact phase evolution and long-term stability under prototypical reactor conditions remain experimentally unvalidated.
